<!-- pr-reviewer: 4b549027f2c8eaf0ec233d419463d9a27a66b293 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** One non-blocking gap on internal (ID) threads is in the notes.

**What looks good**
- Direction and spindle are right. Every pass now falls toward the chuck (`motion/src/turning/thread.rs`, `ccw = hand.ccw_for(true)`). RH is clockwise seen from +Z, so M03. LH is counter-clockwise, so M04. The golden now starts at Z14 and `G76 ... Z8` runs toward the chuck, which matches the PathPilot `M3 / G76 Z-` sample.
- The hand cannot be lost silently. The path from op params to the post:
  - `OpParams::Threading.hand` -> `ThreadParams.hand` -> `ThreadCycle.hand`. `is_sane` holds every XY half-turn to that hand (`cl/thread.rs`).
  - In the stream, `THREAD ... HAND` is required (`cnc_thread.rs` "THREAD needs HAND"), and an unknown or duplicate word is refused.
  - `PARAM SpindleDirection reverse` is emitted whenever the record needs M04.
  - A post script without `threadHands` is refused by name (`engine.rs`).
  - fanuc-lathe refuses a G32 half-turn whose sense disagrees with its spindle, and refuses a G76 record with no hand or with a hand/direction that needs the other spindle (`fanuc-lathe.cps` `threadHalfTurn`, `g76Why`).
  - With no thread record, an LH G32 half-turn under M03 is still refused by the half-turn check, so it fails safe.
- The verdict blocks the post. `thread_hand_warnings` raises a `Gouge` at the first wrong-hand half-turn, wired in `generate.rs`. The motion test pins that the wrong hand is convicted at the first arc.
- Old files load as Right (`#[serde(default)]` on `ParamsDto::Threading.hand` and `ThreadCycleDto.hand`). The default is stated in the field doc comments and in `docs/decisions/629-thread-hand.md`. The cache stamp now includes the hand, so old threading caches go Stale once and regenerate toward the chuck.
- The only golden changed is `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc`: start Z8 -> Z14, G76 end Z14 -> Z8. That is the correct direction.
- The change touches no `build.rs`, scripts, `.github` or dependencies. No snapshot PNGs, no `CHANGELOG.md`. There is a Provenance line, a decision file, a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #629`.

**Local results (merged with upstream/main; it was already up to date, so no conflicts)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| app `turning_thread` | 9 passed |
| app `lathe_post_g76` | 8 passed |
| app `lathe_post_refusals` | 5 passed |
| app `lathe_post` | 7 passed |
| app `lathe_field_tools` | 2 passed |
| app `inverted_post` | 15 passed |
| app `conformance` | 6 passed |
| app `posting` | 17 passed |
| app `golden_cl` | 23 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 69 passed |
| motion `turning_thread` | 18 passed |
| motion `turning_thread_cycle` | 3 passed |
| motion lib | 160 passed |
| post (all targets) | pass |
| cl (all targets) | pass |
| ui lib `thread_hand` | 1 passed |
| clippy `-D warnings` on app, post, motion, cl and ui (`--all-targets`) | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. Acceptance (f) asked for RH and LH pins for OD and ID. RH and LH are pinned (motion `every_pass_runs_toward_the_chuck_and_the_helix_winds_the_asked_hand`; app `lathe_post_g76` RH under M03, LH under M04). Every fixture is an external thread, and `turning/thread.rs` has no internal-thread path. By the screw law the spindle rule is the same for a bore, with the tool on the same side of the axis, so I see no defect. If internal threading is added later it should get its own RH/LH pins.
2. LH is only ever posted as M04, never as M03 away from the chuck. The decision file records this and names the follow-up.
3. #626 (PathPilot lathe post) and the threading stack (#516-#518, #468) must carry `threadHands` and `hand`, as the PR body says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
